ON-01.why: Builds the evidence base for vehicle targets without assigning a new member an entire requirements workstream.
prerequisites: Choose a vehicle with the VSE mentor
Get the current benchmark-row template
Use public, citable sources only
steps: Duplicate one blank benchmark row
Record the vehicle, trim, model year, and source date
Enter each requested metric with units
Link the public source beside each value
Mark unavailable values as a gap rather than guessing
Ask the VSE mentor to review the completed row
ON-01.handoff: Commit or upload the reviewed row in the approved benchmark location and tell the owner which values remain unresolved.

ON-02.why: Proves NX access and the team's basic naming/release workflow before a member touches production CAD.
prerequisites: Complete the Siemens NX setup guide
Confirm the practice-part naming convention
Know where training files are stored
steps: Create a simple bracket or block as a training-only part
Apply the required file name and revision
Add one dimensioned feature
Save to the approved training location
Follow the practice check-in/review/release sequence
Capture the final status and ask the CAD custodian to review it
ON-02.handoff: Submit the part and release screenshot; never place controlled CAD or license information in the public repository.

ON-03.why: Demonstrates that the virtual-vehicle environment opens and produces a reproducible result.
prerequisites: Complete MATLAB and Simulink Onramps
Confirm the required MATLAB release
Receive the approved training model from the PCM mentor
steps: Record MATLAB, Simulink, and add-on versions
Open a fresh copy of the training model
Read its run instructions and expected inputs
Run the model once without changing parameters
Export one labeled result plot
Repeat the run and confirm the result is reproducible
Record warnings or errors exactly
ON-03.handoff: Provide the run log, version list, and labeled plot to the PCM mentor.

ON-04.why: Adds an independent quality check to battery work while preserving battery-design authority.
prerequisites: Select one calculation chain with the battery lead
Use the controlled calculation, not a public copy
Understand the units used
steps: List every input, value, unit, and source
Trace each equation in order
Repeat the arithmetic independently
Check unit conversions and significant figures
Record assumptions and unresolved questions
Compare the result with the controlled calculation
ON-04.handoff: Send a short checked-calculation note to the battery lead; do not edit the source calculation until the lead approves.

ON-05.why: Turns tribal CAD knowledge into a test that future members can follow without verbal rescue.
prerequisites: Choose one CAD workflow step with the NX lead
Read the current instruction
Know the expected end state
steps: Write the action in plain language
State the required input and exact expected result
Add one common failure and recovery step
Include the evidence a reviewer should see
Ask someone unfamiliar with the step to try it
Revise once based on their result
ON-05.handoff: Submit one reviewed acceptance-check entry for inclusion in the CAD onboarding guide.

ON-06.why: Improves compliance while teaching a member how the dashboard relates to controlled requirements.
prerequisites: Choose one deliverable with the PM
Open the latest controlled requirement and scorecard
Open the matching dashboard card
steps: Compare the official date and time
Compare artifact names and formats
Check page, size, naming, and OEM-data limits
Compare the definition-of-done checks
Record every mismatch with the source section
Update only after the accountable owner confirms the correction
ON-06.handoff: Commit one corrected public-safe card or send a no-change verification note with source revision and date.

ON-07.why: Produces visible team storytelling while protecting consent and sensitive information.
prerequisites: Obtain a named MarCom reviewer
Choose a consenting team member
Use approved public-safe facts and images
steps: Ask for written participation and image consent
Collect the approved role and a short quote
Draft concise spotlight copy
Check image dimensions and accessibility text
Remove private, OEM-sensitive, and unapproved claims
Send the complete package for MarCom review
ON-07.handoff: Deliver draft copy, consent record, image specification, and alt text; publication requires named approval.

ON-08.why: Connects research to a verifiable engineering target without assigning architecture authority prematurely.
prerequisites: Choose one vehicle goal with the VSE lead
Collect at least one credible source
Know the target format
steps: Rewrite the goal as one measurable statement
Specify value, unit, operating condition, and boundary
Cite the rationale and source
State how the target will be verified
Identify one uncertainty or tradeoff
Review wording with the VSE lead
ON-08.handoff: Add the approved requirement statement and rationale to the controlled target-development workspace.

ON-09.why: Makes onboarding continuously better and gives a new member a safe first version-controlled change.
prerequisites: Choose an instruction you actually attempted
Reproduce the confusing step
Agree on the smallest useful correction
steps: Describe the user goal
Rewrite the step with an action verb
Add the expected result
Add one likely error and recovery
Test the revision from a clean starting point
Ask a mentor to review before merging
ON-09.handoff: Commit one focused documentation change with a message explaining what confusion it removes.

ON-10.why: Turns an unspoken blocker into an owned, dated coordination item.
prerequisites: Choose a real dependency or pending decision with the PM
Identify the people affected
Find the date when the answer is needed
steps: Write the decision or dependency as one sentence
Record its owner
Record the needed-by date and source
List realistic options or upstream input
State impact if late
Write one next action with a date
ON-10.handoff: Add the reviewed row to the decision or dependency register and notify the affected owner.
